ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the main channel from left to right is the R(s) input, passing through an input branch labeled 1 to the first summing node, then passing through gain K to the second summing node, then passing through the integration element s^{-1} to the third node, and finally outputting Y(s) through the branch labeled 1. From the third node forward there are two feedback/feedforward loops: one returns to the first summing node with gain 1, and the other returns to the second summing node with gain 3. Then reason: according to the method given in the problem, let the variables of the three internal top nodes be x1, x2, and x3 respectively, where x1 is the output of the first summing node after the input gain, x2 is the output of the second summing node after gain K, and x3 is the integrator output. From the figure, write x1 = R + x3, x2 = Kx1 + 3x3, x3 = s^{-1}x2. From x3 = s^{-1}x2, obtain x2 = sx3. Substitute x1 = R + x3 into the x2 equation: sx3 = K(R + x3) + 3x3 = KR + (K + 3)x3. The system characteristic factor is s - (K + 3), corresponding to the pole s = K + 3. Stability of a continuous-time system requires the pole to be located in the left half-plane, so K + 3 < 0, obtaining K < -3.

method.method_draft: After describing the image structure, assign node variables x1, x2, x3 to the three internal top nodes after the input gain, after gain K, and after the integrator. From the diagram write x1=R+x3, x2=Kx1+3x3, and x3=s^{-1}x2. Eliminate x1 and x2: sx3=K(R+x3)+3x3, so the characteristic factor is s-(K+3). Stability requires the pole K+3 to lie in the left half-plane, hence K+3<0, giving K<-3.
